title: A capability carried onward
scope: Proposed execution plan against the live spine. Source inventory headings, curated hall choices and inspected opening evidence; not a claim of 207 tested lessons.

sequences.aim: Build and describe a body from positions, records and faces.
sequences.carry: Recognizable sphere -> endpoints -> retained trace -> grid copy -> face list -> indexed cube -> generated family. Godot Primitives returns to PointBody: holding changes mesh resolution. Keep sphere and cube recipes for later returns toward a capable catalyst.
sequences.check: Build a different small arrangement with a reusable generator; explain position, reference, face and resolution separately.
sequences.note: Finish Trace → Grid before expanding the untested mesh lessons. Keep the last composition free of new syntax.

sequences.aim: Write a changing rule with time, branches, events and retained state.
sequences.carry: The learner's indexed cube retains its established appearance while gaining clock, route, pivot, hierarchy and reset. Transfer a selected transform/action to the familiar sphere as a returning instrument; planks and other museum mechanisms keep their roles.
sequences.check: Make a bounded motion and reset it twice; explain what is recomputed and what is retained.
sequences.note: Sine is a range-and-period preview here. Its circular derivation belongs in Waves. Do not require riding physics to learn interpolation.

sequences.aim: Address and change many independent things.
sequences.carry: Independent copies of the learner's familiar cube become a row, plane and volume. Transfer the same instancing/addressing method to PointBody spheres; preserve each instance's owned resources and explain shared construction versus shared mutable state.
sequences.check: Change one stored value and one object through their indices, preserving unrelated entries; explain aliasing.
sequences.note: Array has no tutorial. This missing foundation precedes sophisticated 3D storage. Split the row and plane into two beats within the hall.

sequences.aim: Separate a calculated value, its receiver and its retained state.
sequences.carry: A colour function becomes a palette object; the returning sphere receives a colour through its owned material. Addressed colour becomes a painted surface; each return adds a capability to a familiar object.
sequences.check: Create two independent palettes, advance one, and apply a returned colour to a new receiver; explain the surface-painting states.
sequences.note: PointBody already introduces a class. Palette deepens methods and owned state; do not call it the first class. Reflection on skin is not reducible to RGB.

sequences.aim: Separate a source from its repeated interpretations.
sequences.carry: A known array and palette become a motif, lookup rule and surface recipe.
sequences.check: Keep the motif fixed while changing one lookup; predict a 4×4 sample and a larger result.
sequences.note: Three ribbon tutorials are missing. One shader lookup can be supplied as a preview; shader execution is taught in its own sequence.

sequences.aim: Distinguish a difference, a rate and an accumulated change.
sequences.carry: The line difference and trace return as measurements of the familiar sphere's positions, a sampled curve and a followed field. Name frame, time interval and units; carry a measurable motion into Forces.
sequences.check: Compare finite differences and finite sums at two step sizes, with units and a retained source.
sequences.note: Field-following assigns a prescribed velocity here. Forces later stores velocity and changes it through acceleration.

sequences.aim: Connect position, velocity, acceleration and applied forces.
sequences.carry: The familiar sphere returns as a flight marker, moving body and interacting mass. Add a named impulse/force response as a step toward the catalyst; preserve its visual recipe and declare each new body/update owner and changed radius or role colour.
sequences.check: Compare the same timed force under two masses; reset and distinguish force, velocity assignment and engine integration.
sequences.note: Reintroduce vector operations through use. A force law is a model; a Godot solver is a supplied implementation with its own contract.

sequences.aim: Change parameters by a criterion rather than draw a desired result directly.
sequences.carry: A body or curve becomes a candidate, evaluated and revised under constraints.
sequences.check: Change a step size or boundary and distinguish convergence, a limit and a failed search.
sequences.note: Annealing needs a small bounded-draw preview before Randomness. Keep current state, best state and evaluator separate.

sequences.aim: Read periodic change in position, time and coupled state.
sequences.carry: A familiar sphere receives periodic position or pulse changes; amplitude, period and phase deepen the earlier motion rule. Carry a reusable oscillator toward catalyst behaviours, then distinguish that body from a sampled wave or coupled field.
sequences.check: Predict amplitude, period and phase changes; combine two known signals and explain the sampling limits.
sequences.note: This sequence owns the unit circle and sine derivation. Sound output, spatial clearance and wave coupling are distinct receivers.

sequences.aim: Make chance reproducible and examine distributions and consequences.
sequences.carry: A rule and seed produce samples, walks, populations and feedback.
sequences.check: Replay a saved recipe; change draw order and compare distributions without claiming identical outcomes across engines.
sequences.note: A short random call can precede this sequence. Here teach the generator, draw order, distributions, sampling policies and inference.

sequences.aim: Sample related values and distinguish the field from its display.
sequences.carry: The sampler drives points, occupancy, skin and route comparisons.
sequences.check: Hold sample positions fixed while changing a generator setting; compare neighbour differences and preserve original values.
sequences.note: Do not infer continuity from smooth colour. Spatial spacing, threshold and domain warp are separate choices.

sequences.aim: Run a small spatial rule for every fragment.
sequences.carry: Known distance, colour, tiling and noise rules move onto a surface.
sequences.check: Write a distance mask, repeat its coordinates, then specify the previous-state input needed to turn a recomputed image into a retained simulation. Do not claim the current display supplies working feedback.
sequences.note: Use The Book of Shaders as an inspiration for operations, translated to Godot. GPU feedback storage is not automatic. Four lessons are missing.

sequences.aim: Give a local rule a stored state and a generation boundary.
sequences.carry: The grid gains current/next buffers, neighbours and recorded generations.
sequences.check: Update a tiny known state by hand, then match it in code; reverse traversal order and preserve the result.
sequences.note: Hall names do not certify algorithms. Verify actual installed rules before calling a specimen elementary CA or Life.

sequences.aim: Describe repeated construction with a stopping rule.
sequences.carry: Known lists and functions become recursive branches and replacement histories.
sequences.check: Predict growth at a small depth and impose a node budget; distinguish recursion depth from physical size.
sequences.note: A visible fractal is not evidence of infinity. Keep base cases and finite budgets explicit.

sequences.aim: Separate rewriting a description from interpreting it.
sequences.carry: A word, stack and recipe construct a branching body.
sequences.check: Rewrite a short word in parallel; copy/restore turtle state at a branch and inspect the resulting connections.
sequences.note: Dictionaries, strings and stacks need explicit small introductions. Shape grammar is currently a missing lesson, not a prerequisite for all growth.

sequences.aim: Keep the representation, evaluator and construction rule visible.
sequences.carry: Candidate records and branch/voxel records generate selections and passages.
sequences.check: Change a fitness criterion or growth condition and explain which candidates or connections it excludes.
sequences.note: Add minimal adjacency at the first network use; Graph Theory later formalizes traversal. Full graph theory need not be moved forward.

sequences.aim: Distinguish a deformable state from the constraints applied to it.
sequences.carry: Mesh vertices and forces become a constrained sheet, pressure body or coupled field.
sequences.check: Hold material and load fixed while changing pinned boundaries; explain solver response versus an authored animation.
sequences.note: Teach a bounded constraint experiment; do not reproduce the full cloth solver in the first lesson.

sequences.aim: Turn sampled scalar values into a chosen boundary.
sequences.carry: A field and a threshold produce a surface and a clearance test.
sequences.check: Classify one cell, interpolate one crossing, then vary level without mutating samples.
sequences.note: Extraction tables are supplied first. Continuous description, finite samples and walkable collision remain distinct.

sequences.aim: Compose solids with ordered set operations.
sequences.carry: Known forms become operands and inhabitable differences.
sequences.check: Swap A−B and B−A; compare with union/intersection and test passage separately from appearance.
sequences.note: Boolean logic already exists. CSG adds solid representations and noncommutative difference, not a fresh introduction to if.

sequences.aim: Give many agents local decisions and shared consequences.
sequences.carry: The moving body gains sensing, steering, neighbours and environmental memory.
sequences.check: Predict one agent update, then compare traversal orders and neighbourhoods in a small population.
sequences.note: Seek/flee/arrive are candidate small studies in the Boids hall; pursuit/evade may remain optional. Do not claim the current lesson already contains them.

sequences.aim: Separate prediction, error and parameter updates.
sequences.carry: An evaluated candidate becomes a model with data, loss and learned weights.
sequences.check: Train on one declared sample set and evaluate on held-out cases; explain what the score cannot establish.
sequences.note: Clustering is not supervised classification. Keep the installed centroid lesson correctly named in the prose. Perceptron/backprop extensions need verified hosts.

sequences.aim: Separate identity and connectivity from drawing positions.
sequences.carry: Known relation records become adjacency, traversals and constrained allocations.
sequences.check: Reconstruct a route from predecessors; test an unreachable target; move the layout without changing connectivity.
sequences.note: Earlier adjacency previews are useful. Here own queues, traversal order, invariants and complexity.

sequences.aim: Distinguish a finite computation, an assumption and a warranted claim.
sequences.carry: Known programs become experiments on geometry, membership and proof checking.
sequences.check: State what a bounded experiment establishes and what it cannot prove; change an assumption explicitly.
sequences.note: Several halls should be reflective investigations with tiny witnesses, not grand algorithms that supposedly demonstrate entire theorems.

sequences.aim: Inspect a proposed research model and its measurement choices.
sequences.carry: Retained observations become weighted expressions and revisable experiments.
sequences.check: Preserve inputs, vary one weight, compare a stated measure and record the interpretive limit.
sequences.note: QFEP is the project’s research proposal. Do not promote a convenient scalar or metaphor into an established physical law.

sequences.aim: Make a revisable work with accountable records and other people.
sequences.carry: Known objects, relations and recipes become situated assemblies and recoverable versions.
sequences.check: Compose an original work, retain its source/decisions and explain whose observations or participation are absent.
sequences.note: This is synthesis and critical reflection. Do not add new compulsory syntax simply to make every hall a lesson.
